actor: Trust-and-safety policy lead, frontier general-purpose model provider
job: Drafting a published usage-policy carve-out that lets identity-verified incident responders submit malware, exploit chains and payload-bearing logs.
outcome: Public documentation naming an enrollable defender program, its eligibility bar, and the cyber-safety refusals lifted for enrolled traffic.
motivation: Case-by-case goodwill scales badly and leaves the provider blamed whenever refusal filters bind the victim's responders instead of the intruder.

task.who: Policy and usage-guidelines team with legal counsel
task.what: Draft published defender exemption to cyber-safety usage policy
task.where: Usage policies, model spec and API terms
task.why: Undocumented per-customer exceptions do not scale
task.how: Written eligibility criteria, attestations, revocation and audit terms

actor: Identity-verification and enrollment product manager, frontier model API platform
job: Building the application, organization-identity checks and entitlement grant that put verified incident responders into a defender tier before an incident.
outcome: A self-serve enrollment lane a responder can find and apply to, granting an account-level entitlement that survives audit.
motivation: An allowlist quietly extended to a few named customers does not answer responders who arrive mid-incident with nowhere to apply.

task.who: API platform product with identity and compliance engineering
task.what: Ship verified-responder enrollment and account entitlement flow
task.where: Developer console, organization settings and account provisioning system
task.why: A findable lane beats mid-incident escalation
task.how: Business-identity verification vendor, org-level entitlements, signed responder attestation

actor: Safety-systems engineering lead, model policy and refusal infrastructure
job: Rebuilding cyber-safety refusals to key on the calling account's entitlement rather than on payload content alone, without weakening the default.
outcome: An entitlement-aware refusal path accepting malware and exploit chains from enrolled accounts while holding the default policy for everyone else.
motivation: Filters that key on content bind the responder and not the intruder, so the exemption must live in the serving path.

task.who: Safety classifier and inference-serving engineering teams
task.what: Make cyber-safety refusals conditional on account entitlement
task.where: Moderation classifiers and request-authorization layer of the API
task.why: Content-keyed filters block defenders, not attackers
task.how: Per-key policy flags, scoped entitlements, differential eval suites

actor: Cyber threat-intelligence and red-team liaison, frontier model provider
job: Setting the vetting bar, abuse monitoring and revocation rules that make a payload-submission exemption hard enough to obtain to survive review.
outcome: A vetted pilot with named incident-response teams, plus published abuse controls letting the program launch instead of stalling in review.
motivation: An enrollment lane is an attacker's lane too, and a configuration setting was all that separated an eval harness from an intrusion.

task.who: Threat intelligence with red team and enforcement
task.what: Define vetting bar and abuse controls for enrollment
task.where: Pilot program with vetted incident-response and CERT partners
task.why: The exception must be hard to obtain
task.how: Adversarial review, usage telemetry, revocation triggers, partner references

actor: Incident-response lead, breached platform security operations
job: Publishing forensics that name hosted-API refusals as the blocker, and filing payload-submission exemption as a requirement with API vendors.
outcome: Named, documented demand from credible defenders that a provider can point at when justifying an enrollable exemption lane.
motivation: A victim that cannot point the best tooling at its own artifacts discloses later and vaguer, and pays for it publicly.

task.who: Security operations, forensics and vendor-management functions
task.what: File payload-submission exemption requirement with hosted API vendors
task.where: Public incident write-ups and enterprise API contract review
task.why: Refusals forced forensics onto open-weight models
task.how: Open-weight fallback tooling, contract terms, public post-incident reports
